claims.text: A 54-year-old man with hypertension, chronic alcohol-related illness and a prior right-hemispheric stroke with residual left spastic hemiparesis/Babinski sign had a brief loss of consciousness at 13:30. Severe aphasia, confusion and agitation followed (NIHSS 7); seizure was suspected but no convulsion signs were detected. IV clonazepam and tiapride treated agitation. Imaging showed only chronic infarction and no acute hemorrhage or arterial occlusion; sodium was 122 mmol/L.

evidence.quote: A 54-year-old man
A 54-year-old man was transported to our department with a suspicion of an epileptic seizure.
According to his mother, the patient lost consciousness for a few minutes at 1:30 p.m. on the day of admission.
After that, he was confused and disoriented, and his speech was unintelligible.

In addition to the moderate-severe left-sided spastic hemiparesis and Babinksi sign due to the previous stroke, severe mixed aphasia and extreme agitation were found during the physical examination (NIHSS: 7 points).
